Prior to the Commencement of the above ground works, updated drainage calculations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The calculations shall take account of all the soft landscaping areas proposed and permeable paving areas within the Surface Water Drainage Scheme Report Appendix B and include: (a) details to demonstrate how the surface water run-off generated up to and including the 100 years critical storm plus climate change allowance, will not exceed the run-off from the undeveloped Site following the corresponding rainfall event. (b) details of modelled drained area and storage structures, together with a detailed drainage layout drawing that show the pipe numbers, gradients and pipe sizes which aligns with the drainage calculations results. In addition, 'brownfield' major developments are required to reduce post development runoff rates for events up to and including the 1 in 100 year return period event plus 40% climate change allowance, to the calculated greenfield rate (calculated in accordance with IoH124) or, where demonstrated not feasible, to not more than three times the calculated greenfield rates for the Site. It is recommended that a SuDS treatment train is utilised to assist in this reduction. Each Phase of the Development shall only be implemented in accordance with the relevant approved details. Prior to occupation of the development evidence (photographs and installation contracts) shall be submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the Site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details and retained for the lifetime of the development. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components. Reason: To safeguard the public from surface water flood risk, protect the environment and respond to climate change, in accordance with Policies SI12 and SI13 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the development a schedule of materials and sample boards for all external facing materials (which for the avoidance of doubt shall also include hard landscaping) to be used in the construction of the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The sample boards should include: Brick and mortar type including mortar joint profile cladding;Window / door types (including frame profile, frame finish, glass types and any manifestation);Balustrades;Metalwork;Soffit materials (e.g. balconies); and, Balcony and terrace floor finishes. Mock-ups of facades shall be provided at a size to be agreed with the Local Planning Authority for each relevant part of the development. These should capture the following areas of the façade as a minimum: Head, jamb and sill details, including profiles, for a typical balcony opening, including balustrade, soffits and terrace floor finishes and glazing; and, Brick elements and mortar joint profile.The development shall thereafter be constructed and retained in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To secure high-quality design and detailing and to ensure that the appearance of the building and details achieves a high standard of design in accordance with LP Plan Policy D9 and SLP Policy 28 and 29.

Prior to commencement of the above ground works, technical details of the selected exhaust air heat pump (EAHP) system, including details of the integrated cooling element must be submitted as appropriate to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing in order to ensure that the development is future-proofed against overheating risks due to future climate scenarios.  Reason: To comply with London Plan SI 4 and Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement prepared by HTA Sustainable Futures Ltd and dated August 2025 together with the approved cooling coil details. Prior to first occupation residential units, 'as-built' Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) outputs must be submitted as appropriate to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that development has achieved the targeted reduction in CO2 emissions, together with documentary evidence to show that the proposed solar PV panels and Exhaust Air Heat Pump (EAHP) units have been implemented on site in accordance with the approved plans. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with London Plan Policy SI 2, SI 3, the Mayor's Energy Assessment guidance and Local Plan Policy 31.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved TM59 Overheating Risk Assessment prepared by HTA Design Ltd and dated August 2025. Prior to first occupation of the residential units, documentary evidence, including finalised TM59 dynamic thermal modelling results must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing, which demonstrates that the cooling strategy has been implemented in line with the approved details. Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 33 2018 and London Plan Policy SI 4 2021
